title: Improved cryopreservation of cardiomyocyte aggregates differentiated from GMP iPSC in a 3D culture format.
cell_types: R26 HLA-homozygous GMP iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte aggregates
study_design: Primary comparison and optimization of commercial/basic freezing media and Y-27632 pre-treatment for 3D cardiomyocyte aggregates, with recovery, purity, viability, morphology, and contraction endpoints.
interventions: Study-labeled 10% HSA condition with CryoSure and final 10% DMSO
10 µM Y-27632 for 1 h before freezing

experiments.model: Cardiomyocyte aggregates from GMP iPSC differentiation days 9–11, >85% ACTN2/TNNT2
experiments.intervention: Commercial media and basic media including 10% HSA, CS-10, Stemdiff-CMFM, Nutrifreeze-D10, Stem Cellbanker, CMFreeze, KOSR variants
experiments.comparator: Fresh aggregate sample and among tested cryomedia
experiments.cooling: Cool cells to 4 °C for 30 minutes; keep near 4 °C while adding medium; CoolCell overnight at −80 °C
experiments.warming: 37 °C water bath until small ice clump; stepwise dilution using pre-cooled 5% HSA solution; two PBS washes
experiments.storage: Liquid nitrogen after overnight −80 °C; study-specific duration not established here
experiments.outcome_name: Aggregate morphology, viability, recovery, and cardiac marker expression
experiments.result: Day-5 cell recovery relative to prefreeze counts was 91.2 ± 50.1% for HSA/CryoSure, 71.2 ± 34.2% for CS10 and 67.3 ± 33.2% for 10% KOSR; several other media were lower. Immediate recoveries near 110% in HSA and 10% KOSR reflect uncertain aggregate counting, not demonstrated cell generation during thawing. Media comparison has high batch variability.
experiments.sample_size: One R26 line; n=8 experiments for HSA, CS10, Stemdiff-CMFM and KOSR conditions; n=5 for three other media; >30 aggregate diameter measurements per experiment
experiments.source_locator: Results, Efficient cryopreservation of cardiomyocyte-aggregates; Fig. 3
experiments.evidence_excerpt: Freezing media CS-10 and 10% HSA demonstrated superior protection

experiments.model: Cryopreserved cardiomyocyte aggregates after 5-day post-thaw culture
experiments.intervention: Additional 1 h pretreatment with 10 µM Y-27632 at 37 °C before HSA/CryoSure freezing
experiments.cooling: Cool cells to 4 °C for 30 minutes; keep near 4 °C while adding medium; CoolCell overnight at −80 °C
experiments.warming: 37 °C water bath until small ice clump; stepwise dilution using pre-cooled 5% HSA solution; two PBS washes
experiments.storage: Liquid nitrogen after overnight −80 °C; study-specific duration not established here
experiments.result: Pretreated recovery was 108.6 ± 47.2% immediately and 75.0 ± 43.8% on day 5, not significantly improved over the same formulation without pretreatment. Morphology appeared more intact immediately, but apoptosis/live-cell measures did not significantly improve. Both groups received post-thaw ROCK inhibition.
experiments.sample_size: n=8 for the Fig. 4 recovery condition
experiments.source_locator: Results, Effect of Y-27632 pre-incubation; Fig. 4
experiments.evidence_excerpt: the 1 h pre-treatment of cells at 37 °C

experiments.model: Cryopreserved cardiomyocyte aggregates assessed by MUSCLEMOTION
experiments.intervention: HSA/CryoSure cryopreservation with versus without extra Y-27632 pretreatment
experiments.comparator: No pretreatment under the same freezing/recovery workflow; fresh age-matched aggregates provide a separate context
experiments.cooling: Cool cells to 4 °C for 30 minutes; keep near 4 °C while adding medium; CoolCell overnight at −80 °C
experiments.warming: 37 °C water bath until small ice clump; stepwise dilution using pre-cooled 5% HSA solution; two PBS washes
experiments.storage: Liquid nitrogen after overnight −80 °C; study-specific duration not established here
experiments.timepoint: 5 days post-thaw; stimulation at 0.5 and 1 Hz
experiments.result: On day 5, spontaneous beating was 10 ± 3 bpm without extra pretreatment and 17 ± 4 bpm with it; both groups paced at 0.5 Hz and partly at 1 Hz. Fresh age-matched aggregates showed no spontaneous and little induced beating. This demonstrates post-thaw beating and a timing-associated difference, not equivalence to mature fresh cardiomyocytes.
experiments.sample_size: n=3 experiments; >40 aggregates measured per experiment
experiments.source_locator: Results, Functionality assessment; Fig. 5 and Extended Data Videos

main_finding: In one R26 iPSC line, the HSA/CryoSure condition had the highest reported mean day-5 cell recovery (91.2 ± 50.1%), with high batch variability. Added Y-27632 pretreatment did not significantly improve recovery or apoptosis outcomes, although spontaneous beating rate differed.
limitations: One R26 donor line; independent experiments/aggregate measurements do not establish multi-donor replication.
Recovery uses a prefreeze cell-count denominator; aggregate dissociation/counting uncertainty can produce values above 100%. Day-5 recovery also includes intervening culture effects.

The condition labeled 10% HSA contains final 10% DMSO from CryoSure. Table 2 describes HSA (20%) input plus CryoSure; exact mass/volume interpretation of the label needs source clarification before replication.
All conditions receive 10 µM Y-27632 during the first 48 h of post-thaw culture; pretreatment comparison tests additional timing, not all ROCK inhibition versus none.
High dispersion (day-5 recovery SD 50.1 percentage points) limits generalization of the highest observed mean. No absolute superiority or equivalence is established across cell formats.
Fresh age-matched aggregates showed no spontaneous and little induced beating; post-thaw beating is not a matched demonstration of unchanged mature cardiac function.
mechanism_claim: The study directly measures process recovery, structure, viability, markers, and contraction; HSA-mediated protection is a formulation interpretation, not proof of a specific biological pathway.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root methods/results and endpoint-definition review

title: Cryopreservation alters contractile function of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes.
study_design: Fresh versus cryopreserved hiPSC-CM comparison using CryoStor CS10 or KSR, followed by recovery, morphology, sarcomeric expression, and paced-contractility measurements at day 10 and day 35.
interventions: KnockOut Serum Replacement (KSR) with 10% DMSO, 10 µM Y-27632, and 10 µL/mL Pluronic-F68

experiments.model: Human hiPSC-CMs differentiated in suspension to day 11–13 and recovered after cryostorage
experiments.intervention: CryoStor CS10 or KSR cryopreservation at −150 °C
experiments.warming: 37 °C water bath until small ice layer remained
experiments.storage: 6 weeks to 6 months; KSR samples 3 and 6 months
experiments.timepoint: Immediate post-thaw recovery; separate purity measurements around days 10 and 35 after plating
experiments.result: Average viable-cell recovery was 39% for CS10 and 46% for KSR. Cardiomyocyte fraction at day 10/day 35 was 61%/64% for CS10 and 83%/79% for KSR versus fresh 81%/80%.
experiments.sample_size: 3 CS10 vials and 2 KSR vials from 2 differentiations; cell-level n varies by assay
experiments.source_locator: Results, Both cryopreservation media have a comparable recovery rate; Fig. 1

experiments.model: Recovered hiPSC-CMs on laminin-coated glass coverslips
experiments.intervention: CS10 or KSR cryopreservation followed by culture
experiments.outcome_name: Cell area, sarcomere length, and myofibril alignment
experiments.result: Cryopreservation increased cell area at day 10 in both media; CS10 remained larger at day 35 while KSR returned closer to fresh. Sarcomere length and alignment also differed by medium and timepoint. Cell-level n was from two differentiations, with alignment score N=1.
experiments.sample_size: cell-level n from two differentiations; alignment score N=1
experiments.source_locator: Results, Cryopreservation alters cell morphology and sarcomere length; Fig. 2

experiments.model: Recovered hiPSC-CMs paced at 1 Hz and analyzed by edge detection
experiments.outcome_name: Contraction amplitude, time to peak, half-relaxation, shortening and relaxation velocity
experiments.result: At day 10, CS10 showed increased twitch amplitude and shorter time-to-peak/half-relaxation, while KSR was comparable to fresh. At day 35, both cryopreserved groups had reduced twitch amplitude and shorter time-to-peak/half-relaxation versus fresh. Analysis used 15–20 twitches per cell, with cell-level n from 3 CS10 and 2 KSR vials across 2 differentiations. Cell-level statistics use nested measurements; unchanged velocity in most comparisons does not imply all contractile features are preserved.
experiments.sample_size: 15–20 twitches averaged per cell; cell-level n from 3 CS10 and 2 KSR vials, 2 differentiations
experiments.source_locator: Results, Cryopreservation alters contractile parameters; Fig. 5 and Methods Contractility

main_finding: CS10 and KSR yielded similarly low recovery, but cryopreservation altered hiPSC-CM morphology and paced contractile parameters in medium- and time-dependent ways.
limitations: Recovery is live cells after thaw divided by the number frozen; it is not live fraction among post-thaw cells. Underlying vial counts are not available for independent recomputation.
One female-donor Phoenix line at passages 43/44 across two differentiations; cell/twitch observations are nested within three CS10 and two KSR vials.
Fresh and recovered cells were grown for corresponding intervals after plating, with different storage histories. Single-cell analyses do not establish donor-level population effects.
Both media have 10% DMSO; KSR additionally has Y-27632 and Pluronic-F68, so the comparison does not isolate one ingredient.
Methods say counts were subtracted but the explicit recovery equation and Figure 1 define a ratio; use the equation and retain the wording discrepancy.
Underlying data are available on author request, not independently reanalyzed here.
mechanism_claim: The study directly measures recovery, morphology, sarcomeric features, and contractility; it demonstrates phenotype alteration after cryopreservation without identifying a single causal injury pathway.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root methods/results and endpoint-definition review
